title: Part 3 Practice: Soil Degradation and Erosion Control Measures

options: A) The improvement of soil quality over time
B) The decline in soil quality, fertility, and productivity due to natural processes and human activities
C) The formation of new soil from parent material
D) The process of adding nutrients to soil
questions.correct_answer: B) The decline in soil quality, fertility, and productivity due to natural processes and human activities
questions.explanation: Correct: Soil degradation is the deterioration of soil quality. A is wrong—degradation is decline, not improvement. C is wrong—this is soil formation. D is wrong—this is fertilization.

questions.text: Which type of soil degradation involves the compression of soil particles reducing pore space?
questions.explanation: Correct: Compaction is physical degradation that compresses soil particles. A is wrong—acidification is chemical degradation. C is wrong—salinization is chemical degradation. D is wrong—nutrient depletion is chemical degradation.

questions.text: Approximately how much soil does Ethiopia lose annually due to erosion?
questions.explanation: Correct: Ethiopia loses 1-2 billion tons of soil annually. A is wrong—too low. C is wrong—too high. D is wrong—still too low; the figure is in billions.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cause of soil degradation in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Correct: Deforestation is a major cause of soil degradation by removing protective cover. A is wrong—afforestation prevents degradation. C is wrong—contour plowing is a conservation measure. D is wrong—terracing is a conservation measure.

questions.text: What type of soil degradation is characterized by the loss of organic matter and decline in soil biodiversity?
questions.explanation: Correct: Biological degradation involves loss of organic matter and biodiversity. A is wrong—physical degradation includes compaction and erosion. C is wrong—chemical degradation includes nutrient depletion and acidification. D is wrong—erosion is physical degradation.

questions.text: Which Ethiopian region is famous for successful soil conservation through integrated approaches?
questions.explanation: Correct: Tigray is famous for successful soil conservation with community participation. A is wrong—Afar is arid with limited conservation. C is wrong—Ogaden is pastoral with different challenges. D is wrong—Kaffa focuses on coffee production.

questions.text: Which of the following is a biological control measure for soil erosion?
questions.explanation: Correct: Agroforestry is a biological measure using trees with crops. A is wrong—terracing is a physical measure. B is wrong—stone bunds are physical measures. D is wrong—check dams are physical measures.

questions.text: What percentage of Ethiopia's highlands are significantly eroded?
questions.explanation: Correct: About 50% of the highlands are significantly eroded. A is wrong—too low. B is wrong—still too low. D is wrong—too high; though severe, not 75%.

questions.text: Chemical degradation of soil includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Correct: Compaction is physical degradation, not chemical. A is wrong—nutrient depletion is chemical. B is wrong—acidification is chemical. C is wrong—salinization is chemical.

questions.text: The success of soil conservation in Tigray demonstrates that:
options: A) Conservation is impossible in Ethiopia
B) Community participation and integrated approaches can reverse degradation
C) Only modern machinery can save soils
D) Conservation is not economically viable
questions.correct_answer: B) Community participation and integrated approaches can reverse degradation
questions.explanation: Correct: Tigray's success proves community action works. A is wrong—Tigray shows it's possible. C is wrong—traditional methods proved effective. D is wrong—conservation is economically beneficial.
